dataset_note: Educational decision-support demonstrator. All telemetry generated by this application is synthetic. The numeric operational bands below are demo configuration values supplied for the challenge brief; they are not represented as a transcription of NASA-STD-3001, NASA flight rules, or an individual's medical prescription. Validate all limits and procedures against current controlled mission documentation before operational use.

co2_mmhg.label: Cabin partial pressure of CO2 (ppCO2)
co2_mmhg.context: The demonstrator uses the challenge brief's operational bands. Verify actual exposure-duration constraints and current mission flight rules.

radiation_msv_hr.label: Ionizing radiation dose rate
radiation_msv_hr.caution: Elevated above nominal; SPE alert reference > 2.0
radiation_msv_hr.context: Dose-rate alerting and career exposure limits depend on mission policy, dosimetry, and current standards; this is not a personal exposure assessment.

heart_rate_bpm.label: Resting heart rate
heart_rate_bpm.context: Challenge-brief flight-baseline band; interpret against crewmember context and operational procedure.

hrv_rmssd_ms.label: Heart-rate variability (RMSSD)
hrv_rmssd_ms.caution: Outside 28–65 or > 30% below personal pre-flight baseline
hrv_rmssd_ms.context: Challenge-brief reference range. A personal trend is more informative than a population range.

spo2_pct.label: Arterial oxygen saturation (SpO2)
spo2_pct.context: Challenge-brief thresholds. Confirm sensor fit, perfusion, and measurement quality before escalation.

core_temp_c.label: Core body temperature
core_temp_c.context: Challenge-brief bands; use the approved measurement method and medical procedure.

glucose_mg_dl.label: Spot blood glucose
glucose_mg_dl.context: Challenge-brief reference band; not an individualized treatment target.

sans_amsler.label: SANS visual Amsler-grid check
sans_amsler.nominal: No new distortion, missing areas, or asymmetry reported
sans_amsler.caution: Any new visual change requires prompt reporting
sans_amsler.context: Qualitative screening prompt only; it is not a diagnostic test or substitute for an approved ocular examination.

biomarker_sops.name: 12-Lead / Wearable ECG & HRV
biomarker_sops.sensor_hardware: Approved wearable ECG recorder or mission-qualified 12-lead ECG, skin electrodes, and the validated onboard analysis application.
protocol: Confirm the crew member, device identity, battery, and the current approved measurement schedule.
Rest in the posture specified by the onboard medical checklist; avoid talking or unnecessary movement during acquisition.
Prepare skin and place electrodes according to the device diagram; verify lead contact and signal-quality indicators.
Acquire the scheduled trace and RR series for the device-prescribed duration. Repeat only when the approved procedure permits and the signal is poor.
Review symptoms and the displayed trend with the crew member; record acquisition time, posture, activity, and signal quality.
Report symptoms or an abnormal trace through the onboard medical checklist and communications plan; do not self-diagnose from this display.
biomarker_sops.pathophysiology: Autonomic tone, sleep disruption, workload, fluid shifts, illness, and stress can alter heart rate and beat-to-beat variability. Rhythm interpretation requires trained clinical review and a validated ECG system.
biomarker_sops.cadence: Use the mission medical schedule; increase sampling only when directed by the onboard medical checklist or flight surgeon.
biomarker_sops.limits: HR 55–85 bpm; RMSSD 28–65 ms demo reference. Flag a >30% RMSSD decrease from the personal pre-flight baseline for review.

biomarker_sops.name: Pulse Oximetry SpO2
biomarker_sops.sensor_hardware: Mission-qualified pulse oximeter with compatible finger/ear probe and displayed signal/perfusion-quality indicator.
protocol: Check the instrument status and select the crew member profile specified by the medical checklist.
Seat the probe fully on the approved site; keep the hand still and warm, and remove avoidable optical obstruction.
Wait for a stable pulse waveform and signal-quality indicator before recording the value.
Record SpO2, pulse rate, time, body position, symptoms, and signal quality together.
If the reading is unexpected, check probe placement and repeat once as allowed by the checklist; report persistent abnormal values or symptoms promptly.
biomarker_sops.pathophysiology: Cabin atmosphere, suit systems, cardiopulmonary status, perfusion, and sensor fit affect oxygenation readings. A single low-quality sample can be misleading; symptoms and trend matter.
biomarker_sops.cadence: At scheduled medical checks and whenever directed by the onboard medical checklist for symptoms or a system event.
biomarker_sops.limits: 96–100% demo nominal; <92% demo acute alert threshold. Use current mission procedure for response.

biomarker_sops.name: Core Thermal Pill / Tympanic
biomarker_sops.sensor_hardware: Mission-qualified ingestible core-temperature sensor with receiver, or approved tympanic thermometer and single-use cover.
protocol: Use only the measurement method and device authorized by the current onboard medical checklist.
For a thermal pill, verify sensor pairing and timing instructions before ingestion; never reuse an ingestible sensor.
For tympanic measurement, fit the approved cover, position the probe as shown in the device instructions, and obtain the prescribed repeat if required.
Record the value, method, time, recent activity, suit/workload context, and associated symptoms.
If heat illness is suspected or a critical value appears, follow the approved stabilization and EVA/suit contingency procedure and notify the responsible crew member.
biomarker_sops.pathophysiology: Heat load, exercise, hydration, illness, and suit cooling performance influence thermal balance. Microgravity changes heat and sweat distribution; sensor method and timing matter.
biomarker_sops.cadence: Follow scheduled checks and EVA/suit thermal monitoring procedures; additional measurement is by checklist or flight-surgeon direction.
biomarker_sops.limits: 36.5–37.5 °C demo nominal; >38.5 °C demo EVA thermal emergency reference.

biomarker_sops.name: Capillary Blood Glucose
biomarker_sops.sensor_hardware: Mission-qualified glucose meter, compatible test strip, approved lancet, gloves, and biohazard sharps/waste container.
protocol: Confirm the meter and strip lot/status and follow the approved infection-control and sharps procedure.
Wash or clean and fully dry the approved sampling site as specified by the device instructions.
Use a new approved lancet and strip; obtain the sample exactly as trained and keep the strip port clean.
Read the meter only after its quality/status indicator confirms a valid result; dispose of sharps and biohazard waste per checklist.
Record the value, time, relation to meal/activity if requested, symptoms, and meter status; report unexpected values rather than changing treatment.
biomarker_sops.pathophysiology: Nutrition, stress hormones, exercise, illness, and medication can affect glucose regulation. Microgravity-associated workload and schedule changes make context and trend important.
biomarker_sops.cadence: Only at the mission-scheduled interval or when directed by the medical checklist; follow individualized clinician instructions.
biomarker_sops.limits: 70–140 mg/dL demo reference only; treatment targets are individualized and are not provided by this application.

biomarker_sops.name: Active Personal Dosimeter
biomarker_sops.sensor_hardware: Mission-qualified personal active dosimeter, assigned crew ID, functioning battery, and approved radiation-monitoring interface.
protocol: Verify assignment, calibration/status indicator, time synchronization, and alarm configuration against the mission checklist.
Wear the dosimeter at the specified body location and orientation; do not shield, exchange, or remove it except as directed.
Check displayed dose and dose rate at scheduled intervals and after a radiation alarm or event.
Record the event time, location/activity, displayed dose/rate, and device status; preserve device data for the radiation officer.
For an alarm or SPE notification, follow the approved shelter/mission procedure immediately and notify the designated authority.
biomarker_sops.pathophysiology: Space radiation includes variable galactic cosmic-ray and solar-particle contributions. Dose rate can change rapidly during a solar particle event; individual exposure assessment requires the mission dosimetry system.
biomarker_sops.cadence: Wear continuously when directed; review per mission radiation-monitoring cadence and after alarms/events.
biomarker_sops.limits: <0.02 mSv/hr demo nominal; >2.0 mSv/hr demo SPE alert reference; 600 mSv is the challenge-brief career PEL reference, not a per-event threshold.

biomarker_sops.name: SANS Visual Amsler Grid Check
biomarker_sops.sensor_hardware: Approved printed or electronic Amsler grid, mission-approved near-vision correction, and adequate uniform illumination.
protocol: Use the approved grid at the specified viewing distance with usual near-vision correction.
Cover one eye without pressing on it; keep gaze fixed on the center mark while noticing any missing, wavy, blurred, or distorted areas.
Repeat for the other eye and compare with the crew member's documented baseline using the prescribed recording method.
Record eye, time, correction used, and the crew member's description; do not infer a diagnosis from the grid.
Report any new visual change promptly for clinician review under the current ocular-health checklist.
biomarker_sops.pathophysiology: Spaceflight-associated neuro-ocular changes can involve fluid shifts and ocular structure/vision changes. A simple grid is only a symptom-screening aid and cannot determine cause.
biomarker_sops.cadence: Use the mission medical schedule and any additional interval directed by the ocular-health checklist or flight surgeon.
biomarker_sops.limits: Qualitative only. Any new distortion, missing area, or asymmetric change is a report-and-review trigger, not a diagnosis.
